reviews.body: Please see my comments and thanks again for contributing!

review_comments.body: Same events would be published multiple times on retry which is not ideal.

The WorkPlacement controller doesn't write this annotation. I think a `kratix.io/` key and a `workplacement-controller` value make it look like a real behaviour which is a little misleading. Could we use a name that is obviously test-only?

comments.body:
@pcbeingused333 thanks for your contribution! I think there are couple more places in the scheduler that are updating the workplacement status and could benefit from a retry on conflict, for example: https://github.com/syntasso/kratix/blob/b4f7bfe25a9b30f5d13579591c14ca3089783e2b/internal/controller/scheduler.go#L489 and https://github.com/syntasso/kratix/blob/b4f7bfe25a9b30f5d13579591c14ca3089783e2b/internal/controller/scheduler.go#L519

Could you please address them in this PR as well? Thanks!

Thanks @ChunyiLyu, good catch. Both `Status().Update` calls you pointed at (misplaced and scheduled branches in `updateWorkPlacementStatus`) now go through `retry.RetryOnConflict`: the function re-reads the WorkPlacement on each attempt and recomputes the conditions before writing. I added a spec that injects a 409 on the status update and checks the reconcile succeeds and the conditions are written; it fails without the change.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Thanks @ChunyiLyu, all four addressed: the spec update now reads straight into `workPlacement`; the misplaced Warning event is published once after the retry loop instead of per attempt; the test annotation is now `test-only/simulated-concurrent-write` with value `simulated`; and the comment in the interceptor is replaced with your wording.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
